To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the age of 70 Ophil is 6.2 Gyr, that the initial composition is (Yi,Zi/X)i = (0.266,0.0300) and that the value of αMLT is lower or equal than the solar calibrated value.
70 Ophi A and B are both old (about 6.2 Gyr), metal-poor (Z = 0.01) and helium-rich (Y = 0.27), and that 70 Oph B is a low-mass star (0.8 M⊙) that is now in the helium-burning phase.

70 Oph is a 6.2 Gyr old binary system, that 70 Ophi A is a 1.5 M⊙, solar metallicity, ZAMS star with an initial helium abundance Yi = 0,266 and that the value of αMLT is likely to be lower or equal to 1.68.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the 2D solar model obtained by the Garching group, the 3D solar model by the Nice group and the 2D and 3D models obtained by the Meudon group.
the study of the effects of atomic diffusion on the internal structure and evolution of solar-like stars and the determination of the mixing-length calibration.
the determination of the global parameters of a star in a binary system using the new astereseismic measurements now available.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the internal structure of the 70Ophiuchi system is well reproduced by current stellar evolution codes, but that the value of αMLT is still a free parameter.
70 Ophiuchus is a 6.2 ± 1.0-Gyr-old solar twin.
the 70 Oph system is a benchmark for stellar physics and asteroseismology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 70 Oph system provides a stringent test for our knowledge of stellar structure and evolution, which can be passed only by a model that includes atomic diffusion and adopts the solar calibrated value of the mixing length parameter.
the current state of the art of stellar evolution codes and calibration procedures can successfully reproduce the observations of 70 Ophil A.
70 Ophi is a very well determined benchmark for stellar evolution theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of the 2D seismic map of the A component of 70 Ophis is now providing a unique opportunity to test our knowledge on stellar physics.
the current state-of-the-art of stellar evolution codes is able to reproduce all the observational constraints available for 70Ophiuchi AB with a precision better than 2%.

the current seismic constraints are sufficient to determine the global parameters of both stars of the 70Oph system, but that the current seismic observations are not yet precise enough to determine the value of the solar calibrated mixing-length parameter for 70Oph A.
